# Error codes

Every failure carries a stable `code`. Programs branch on the code. The
`message` is written for people and may be reworded between versions.

## Shapes

The API's own routes answer with one envelope:

```json
{ "code": "vault_section_not_writable", "message": "This key or tool cannot write to that section.", "status": 403 }
```

A write to a collection that fails field validation names the fields under
`data`, each with its own code:

```json
{ "status": 400, "message": "Failed to create record.", "data": { "key": { "code": "validation_required", "message": "Cannot be blank." } } }
```

The OpenID Connect endpoints answer `{ "error": …, "error_description": … }`,
as OAuth 2.0 specifies.

## In the JavaScript SDK

Each shape is decoded into one `RevokedError`. Its `code` is the envelope's
code, the OAuth `error`, or the first field's code, in that order. An answer
without any of them has the code `http_<status>`, and a request that got no
answer has `network` or `timeout`. `fields` holds the per-field codes.

| Status | Class |
|---|---|
| 400, 422 | `ValidationError` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationError` |
| 403 | `PermissionError` |
| 404 | `NotFoundError` |
| 409 | `ConflictError` |
| 410 | `GoneError` |
| 413 | `PayloadTooLargeError` |
| 429 | `RateLimitedError`, with `retryAfter` in seconds |
| 5xx | `ServerError` |
| no answer | `NetworkError`, `TimeoutError` |

```ts
import { RevokedError } from '@kiunke.dev/revoked';

try {
  await revoked.vault.create({ key: 'note', value: 'text', section });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof RevokedError && error.code === 'vault_section_not_writable') {
    // the key may not write to that section
  }
  throw error;
}
```

## Codes

The status is set where an error is raised, so the same code can answer with
more than one status. A newer server can send a code missing from this list.

| Code | Message |
|---|---|
| `access_denied` | This action is not permitted on this record. |
| `active_workspace_mismatch` | The selected workspace does not match the active workspace. |
| `alias_cycle` | An alias cannot point at another alias. |
| `alias_parent_missing` | The alias parent record does not exist in this workspace. |
| `already_workspace_member` | This account already has access to this workspace. |
| `api_key_expired` | This API key has expired. |
| `api_key_not_permitted` | This action requires a user session; API keys are not accepted. |
| `api_key_vault_scope` | API keys reach the vault only through assigned sections. At least one section is required. |
| `application_needs_watermark` | An application link must stamp its files. |
| `archive_empty` | This share has no files that can be downloaded together. |
| `attestation_check_closed` | This check was already answered or has expired. |
| `attestation_check_invalid` | A check names a type without spaces, attesters as domains, and claims as names of letters, digits and underscores. |
| `attestation_check_not_found` | This check does not exist. The link may be incomplete. |
| `attestation_claim_reserved` | A claim uses a name the credential format sets itself. |
| `attestation_claims_invalid` | Claims are a flat set of named values: names of letters, digits and underscores, values of text, numbers or true/false. |
| `attestation_expiry_invalid` | The end date of an attestation or offer must be in the future. |
| `attestation_identity_mismatch` | This offer was made for a different identity. |
| `attestation_immutable` | An attestation's statement cannot be changed once issued. It can be revoked and reissued. |
